title: Representational Schema-to-Struct Duplication
pattern: Manually duplicating DB table layouts, columns, and entity relations inside raw string queries and language struct definitions.
why_bad: Changing a database field type or adding a column requires a synchronized manual edit of language structures, serialization tags, and inline queries, causing fragile database mapping errors.
detection: The manual mapping of database field structures in raw string queries matching manual compiled-language structure definitions.
counterexample: Bespoke, hand-crafted queries built strictly for performance optimizations where standard schema validation is unfeasible.
fix: Drive the struct generation and query validation from the database schema itself at build-time using schema validation macros.
source: *The Pragmatic Programmer* (20th Anniversary Edition), Topic 9: "Representational Duplication", p. 204-205.
